description: B2 practice sets for the grammar topics that had none, written by hand (2026-10-13). Imported and published.

lessons.title: It Had Already Started: Past Perfect
lessons.description: Practise the Past Perfect to show which past action happened first.

exercises.prompt: When we arrived at the cinema, the film ___.
exercises.explanation: The film started before we arrived: Past Perfect for the earlier action.

exercises.prompt: She was nervous because she ___ on a plane before.
exercises.explanation: Experience up to a moment in the past: had never been.

exercises.prompt: By the time I got home, my brother ___ (eat) all the pizza.
exercises.explanation: By the time + Past Simple, then Past Perfect for the earlier action.

exercises.prompt: I couldn't log in because I ___ my password.
exercises.explanation: Forgetting happened before trying to log in: Past Perfect.

exercises.prompt: “After she had went home, she called me” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: had + past participle: had gone, not had went.

exercises.prompt: “They had just left when we got there” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: had just + past participle shows the action happened shortly before.
Question: Had + subject + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.

pairs.The shop had closed: so we couldn't buy any snacks.
pairs.I realised that: I had left my bag on the bus.

exercises.explanation: Past Perfect explains what happened earlier in a past story.

exercises.prompt: The teacher asked if we ___ our homework.
exercises.explanation: Something completed before the moment of asking in the past: had done.

exercises.prompt: It was my first time in Rome. I ___ (never / visit) Italy before.
exercises.explanation: Experience before a past moment: had never visited.

lessons.title: If I Had Known…: Third Conditional
lessons.description: Practise the third conditional to talk about past situations that did not happen.

exercises.prompt: If I had known about the party, I ___ .
exercises.explanation: Third conditional: If + had + V3, would have + V3.

exercises.prompt: If she ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
exercises.explanation: The if part uses had + past participle.

exercises.prompt: We would have caught the bus if we ___ (leave) earlier.
exercises.explanation: if + Past Perfect: had left.

exercises.prompt: If you had asked me, I ___ (help) you.
exercises.explanation: Result: would have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: “If I would have seen you, I would have said hello” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: No would in the if part: If I had seen you…

exercises.prompt: “If it hadn't rained, we would have played outside” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Negative if part: hadn't + past participle.
Result first, then if + had + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Match the halves.

pairs.If I had checked the weather,: I would have taken an umbrella.
pairs.If they had played better,: they would have won the match.

exercises.explanation: Each imaginary past condition matches its logical result.

exercises.prompt: What would you have done if you ___ the lottery last year?
exercises.explanation: Imagined past situation: if + had won.

exercises.prompt: I ___ (not / be) late if the train hadn't stopped.
exercises.explanation: Negative result: wouldn't have been.

lessons.title: She Said That…: Reported Speech
lessons.description: Practise reporting statements and questions: tense changes, said vs told.

exercises.prompt: “I am tired.” → She said that she ___ tired.
exercises.explanation: Present Simple becomes Past Simple after said.

exercises.prompt: “I will call you.” → He said he ___ call me.
exercises.explanation: will becomes would in reported speech.

exercises.prompt: He ___ me that he was busy.
exercises.explanation: tell + person (told me); say without a person (said that).

exercises.prompt: “I have finished.” → She said she ___ finished.
exercises.explanation: Present Perfect becomes Past Perfect: had finished.

exercises.prompt: “Where do you live?” → He asked me where I ___ .
exercises.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order; the verb usually moves back a tense: where I lived (live is also possible if it is still true).

exercises.prompt: “She asked me where did I go” is a correct reported question.
exercises.explanation: No question word order: She asked me where I went.

exercises.prompt: “He said that he was going to the gym” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Present Continuous (I am going) becomes Past Continuous (was going).
Yes/no questions are reported with if: asked if I liked.

exercises.prompt: Match direct speech with reported speech.

pairs.“I'm watching TV.”: He said he was watching TV.
pairs.“I saw it.”: He said he had seen it.

exercises.explanation: can → could, am watching → was watching, saw → had seen.

exercises.prompt: “Don't be late!” → Mum told me ___ late.
exercises.explanation: Reported orders: tell someone (not) to + verb.

lessons.title: It Must Be, It Can't Be: Modals of Deduction
lessons.description: Practise must, might, could and can't to say how sure you are.

exercises.prompt: She's been working all day. She ___ be exhausted.
exercises.explanation: We are almost sure it is true: must.

exercises.prompt: That ___ be Tom. He's in Australia right now!
exercises.explanation: We are sure it is impossible: can't.

exercises.prompt: I'm not sure where Anna is. She ___ be at the library.
exercises.explanation: It's possible, but we're not sure: might.

exercises.prompt: He didn't answer his phone. He ___ have been asleep. (must / can't)
exercises.explanation: Past deduction, almost sure: must have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: She ___ have seen the message — her phone was off. (must / can't)
exercises.explanation: Impossible in the past: can't have seen.

exercises.prompt: “He must to be at home” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: No to after must: He must be at home.

exercises.prompt: “They might have missed the bus” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: might have + past participle: a possible past explanation.

exercises.prompt: Match the modal with how sure the speaker is.
exercises.explanation: must → nearly certain; might → possible; can't → impossible.
must have + past participle for a confident guess about the past.

exercises.prompt: The lights are off. They ___ have gone out.
exercises.explanation: The lights off is good evidence: must have gone out.

lessons.title: This Time Tomorrow: Future Continuous and Future Perfect
lessons.description: Practise will be doing and will have done for plans and completed future actions.

exercises.prompt: This time tomorrow I ___ on the beach.
exercises.explanation: An action in progress at a future moment: Future Continuous.

exercises.prompt: By 2030 scientists ___ a cure for this disease.
exercises.explanation: Completed before a future time (by 2030): Future Perfect.

exercises.prompt: Don't call at 8 — we ___ (have) dinner then.
exercises.explanation: In progress at 8: will be having.

exercises.prompt: By the end of the month, I ___ (read) ten books.
exercises.explanation: By + future time, completed: will have read.

exercises.prompt: “By Friday she will have finished the project” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: will have + past participle with by + time.

exercises.prompt: “At midnight I will have sleeping” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: In progress: I will be sleeping.
Polite question about plans: Will you be + -ing?

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: will be -ing = in progress; will have + V3 = completed; will + verb = simple future.

exercises.prompt: In two years I ___ from university.
exercises.explanation: Completed by a future point: will have graduated.

exercises.prompt: Next week at this time, they ___ (fly) to New York.
exercises.explanation: In progress at a future time: will be flying.

lessons.title: It Is Being Built: The Passive in All Tenses
lessons.description: Practise the passive with continuous, perfect and modal forms.

exercises.prompt: A new stadium ___ in our city right now.
exercises.explanation: In progress now: is being + past participle.

exercises.prompt: The results ___ yet.
exercises.explanation: Present Perfect passive: have been + past participle.

exercises.prompt: The homework must ___ by Monday.
exercises.explanation: Modal passive: must be + past participle.

exercises.prompt: The room ___ (clean) when we arrived, so we waited outside.
exercises.explanation: In progress in the past: was being cleaned.

exercises.prompt: The tickets ___ (sell) out before we got there.
exercises.explanation: Past Perfect passive: had been sold.

exercises.prompt: “The video has been watched a million times” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Present Perfect passive: has been + past participle.

exercises.prompt: “The letter will be send tomorrow” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Future passive needs the past participle: will be sent.
going to be + past participle for a planned passive action.

exercises.prompt: Match the tense with the passive form.
exercises.explanation: Each tense keeps its auxiliary and adds be + past participle.

exercises.prompt: This problem ___ solved easily.
exercises.explanation: Modal passive: can be + past participle.

lessons.title: I Wish I Could…: Wish and If Only
lessons.description: Practise wish and if only for present regrets, past regrets and annoying habits.

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ taller.
exercises.explanation: A wish about the present: wish + past (were).

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ to the concert last night. Everyone says it was amazing!
exercises.explanation: A regret about the past: wish + Past Perfect.

exercises.prompt: I wish my neighbours ___ so much noise. It's so annoying!
exercises.explanation: Annoying behaviour we want to change: wish + would(n't).

exercises.prompt: If only I ___ (have) more free time now!
exercises.explanation: Present wish: if only + Past Simple.

exercises.prompt: She wishes she ___ (not / say) that yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Past regret: wish + hadn't + past participle.

exercises.prompt: “I wish I can speak Korean” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: Present wish uses could: I wish I could speak Korean.

exercises.prompt: “If only I had listened to you!” is a correct sentence.
exercises.explanation: If only + Past Perfect for a strong past regret.
wish + would for something we want to change.

exercises.prompt: Match the wish with what it is about.
exercises.explanation: past → present wish; Past Perfect → past regret; would → annoying behaviour.

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ swim. I'd love to go surfing.
exercises.explanation: Ability we don't have now: wish + could.
